title: 41st sitting of the 20th Majlis
presiding: Speaker Abdul Raheem Abdulla (Fonadhoo); Deputy Speaker Ahmed Nazim (Dhiggaru) took the chair partway through the debate on item 7.1
summary: The sitting opened with the Speaker announcing two committee seat swaps and deadlines for committee work, then ministers' question time: the Minister of Homeland Security and Technology, Ali Ihsan, answered members on police stations in the islands, undocumented foreign workers, seized money and valuables, prison scam calls and border monitoring. Two bills (amending the Anti-Corruption Commission Act and the Elections Commission Act) had their first reading. Members then began the preliminary debate on a bill to raise the tobacco sale age from 18 to 21 and ban e-cigarettes and vapes; most speakers backed it, while some MDP members questioned the vape ban, the exemption for heated tobacco and the revenue motive. The debate was still going at the end of this part. The sitting finished the preliminary debate on a bill to amend the Tobacco Control Act, which would restrict where tobacco can be used and raise the minimum age; members argued over vaping among students and over the role of past governments. The Foreign Relations Committee's report on appointing Aishath Azeema as Ambassador to India was debated and members spoke in support. After a break, three votes were held: a one-day extension for the Budget Committee on the 2024 supplementary budget, the ambassador appointment, and acceptance of the tobacco bill, which was sent to the Social Committee.

items.title: Opening prayers and start of the sitting
Attendance of members
items.outcome: 49 present, 3 on official travel reported by the chair

items.title: Changes to committee membership
items.outcome: announced: Velidhoo member Mohamed Abbas to the Economic Committee in place of Meedhoo member Ahmed Siyam Mohamed, who moves to the Petitions Committee

items.title: Deadlines for matters sent to committee, and the budget committee's request for an extra day
items.outcome: Economic Committee deadlines announced (Deputy Commissioner General of Taxation appointment, Copyright Act amendment bill); chair said the extra-day request for the supplementary budget committee would go to a vote at voting time

items.title: Questions to the Minister of Homeland Security and Technology
items.outcome: 12 members asked questions and follow-ups; minister answered each in turn

items.title: First reading: bill to amend the Anti-Corruption Commission Act (Act 2008/13), sponsored by Felidhoo member Adam Zahir
First reading: bill to amend the Elections Commission Act (Act 2008/8), sponsored by Kelaa member Abdulla Shareef
Preliminary debate: bill to amend the Tobacco Control Act (Act 2010/15), sponsored by North Henveyru member Ahmed Aifan
items.outcome: debated; 14 members spoke in this part and the debate continued

items.title: Preliminary debate on the bill to amend the Tobacco Control Act (Act 2010/15), sponsored by Ahmed Aifan
items.outcome: debated; accepted 76-0 with 1 abstention; sent to the Social Committee

items.title: Foreign Relations Committee report on appointing Aishath Azeema as Ambassador to the Republic of India
Votes on matters ready for a vote
items.outcome: 3 votes held: Budget Committee extension passed 80-0; ambassador appointment passed 79-0; tobacco bill accepted 76-0 (1 abstention)

speakers.name: Ali Ihsan
positions: Minister of Homeland Security and Technology: described how seized money is held and audited, and said police services are being set up on 115 islands in priority order.
Said 4,428 undocumented foreign workers had been deported as of last month and a biometric data collection drive is nearly complete.
Said a drafted bill would make anti-drug work permanent, and prisons are adding phone-blocking and scanners against scam calls.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Asked how undocumented foreigners in Velidhoo would be dealt with and when its police station work would begin.
Backed the ambassador report and the government's policy of placing women in senior representative roles; said the MDA fully accepts the report.
On the tobacco bill, said school discipline was stricter in the past and criticised the MDP's record on youth.
After the point of order, said he took the MDP member's concerns seriously but repeated his criticism of the MDP's past role.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Asked about plans for carrying out death sentences, and for police land in his constituency.
On the tobacco bill, asked how vapes became common in schools and linked it to changes in society.
Said the MDP supports the ambassador report and wants women to hold more responsible posts.
Raised a point of order objecting to blaming the MDP, a large party, for the views of youth towards authority.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Asked how the foreign labour system was handed to a Malaysian company, and how seized gold, silver and phones are handled.
On the tobacco bill, raised concern about higher cigarette prices, household budgets, consultation and possible smuggling.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Supported the bill, saying vaping is easy to hide and widespread among children, and backed the President's action.
Presented the Foreign Relations Committee report: the nominee met the legal requirements and the committee agreed unanimously to recommend her.
In closing, welcomed the appointment as a sign of women's growing role in foreign policy.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Asked whether police and customs have a solid system for holding money seized in investigations.
Asked why the ministry had not answered his letters.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Asked how labour disputes are being resolved after the Labour Relations Authority moved under the ministry.
Said MDP supports tobacco control but questioned the bill's link to revenue through import duty and the separate duty bill.

speakers.name: Ahmed Aifan
positions: Presented the bill: protect children and youth, raise the sale age from 18 to 21, and ban importing and selling e-cigarettes and vapes.
As sponsor, said the tobacco bill is about protecting public health and youth, not raising revenue, and urged quick committee passage.

speakers.name: Faruhath Mohamed
positions: Asked when work on a modern police station in Kulhudhuffushi city would start.

speakers.name: Mohamed Dawoodh
positions: Asked when ID card printing would start directly in Kulhudhuffushi.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Asked what benefit deporting undocumented foreigners brings the economy and citizens.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Asked about the policy to strengthen police desks against drugs, and about scam calls allegedly made from prison.

speakers.name: Ahmed Shakir
positions: Asked how well border waters are monitored in real time and about identifying foreigners through biometrics.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Asked whether the minister knew of a company paid under the previous government to build police stations.

speakers.name: Ashraf Rasheed
positions: Asked whether Faresmaathodaa, Fiyoari and Rathafandhoo police stations are in the building plan.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Supported the bill, saying it protects young people, and welcomed the age rise to 21.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Supported the bill, said its aim is not revenue, and urged smokers to cut down or quit.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abdul Rahman
positions: Supported the bill, welcoming steps to keep children away from tobacco and the age rise to 21.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Supported the bill, said opposition claims were political, and cited vape cartridges containing cannabis oil.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Backed parts of the bill but raised concern about property rights, the heated-tobacco exemption, and vapes being less harmful than cigarettes.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Supported the bill and rejected the claim that it is a revenue measure.

speakers.name: Ahmed Zahir
positions: Supported the bill, citing United Kingdom and United States youth vaping figures and the UK vape ban from 2025.

speakers.name: Hussain Hameed
positions: Supported the bill and urged it be sent to committee and passed quickly.

speakers.name: Fathimath Sauda
positions: Supported the bill and hoped the committee would consider addiction treatment and rehabilitation.

decisions: Announced Mohamed Abbas (Velidhoo) joins the Economic Committee and Ahmed Siyam Mohamed (Meedhoo) joins the Petitions Committee.
Announced committee deadlines for the Deputy Commissioner General of Taxation appointment and the Copyright Act amendment bill.
First reading of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act amendment bill read.
First reading of the Elections Commission Act amendment bill read.
Budget Committee given one more day to finish its work on the 2024 supplementary budget (80-0).
Aishath Azeema's appointment as Ambassador to India approved (79-0).
Tobacco Control Act amendment bill accepted at preliminary stage (76-0, 1 abstention) and sent to the Social Committee.
Next sitting set for Tuesday 29 October 2024 at 9:00.

Appointment of Aishath Azeema as Ambassador to the Republic of India
